quoted_clause: The guardrail budget caps total input at 13,000 tokens — a safety margin above the append-only worst case (12,660 at T = 4, Table 19-1), so the turn cap binds before the guardrail does.
observed: 'Total input' is ambiguous. If it means cumulative input across calls, T=1 already sums to 19,265 tokens, far above 13,000. The comparison to 12,660 only makes sense for per-call final context length.
evidence: Table 19-1's 12,660 is 'Retained-context input, final call'; the §8 ledger's T=1 Σ per-call input is 19,265.
root_cause: The guardrail is described as a total-input cap but compared to a per-call context length.
correction: Say 'caps per-call input context at 13,000 tokens' or 'caps the final-call context at 13,000 tokens'; if the guardrail is cumulative, recompute the binding point.
acceptance_test: State the guardrail's unit and interval; verify 13,000 against the same quantity (per-call vs cumulative).

quoted_clause: The scheduling unit is the whole request, not the model call: the request holds its KV slot across every tool round-trip, so a T = 3 request occupies capacity for W ≈ 17.70 s even though the GPU is idle for the tool legs — concurrency is set by wall-clock occupancy, not by GPU-busy time.
observed: This is presented as a universal architecture consequence, but it depends on the stated no-reuse/hold-KV policy. Systems that offload, swap, or free KV during tool waits would not have concurrency set by full wall-clock occupancy.
evidence: The chapter's own policy says no prefix cache is reused and the request holds its KV slot; other serving designs can offload KV.
root_cause: A policy-dependent statement is written as a general law.
correction: Qualify: 'Under the stated hold-KV/no-reuse policy...' and note that KV offload/swap changes the occupancy calculation.
acceptance_test: Check whether the sentence is true under alternative KV-offload policies; if not, add the qualifier.

quoted_clause: Under this convention the 2% fallback is a high-tail/failure category that incurs zero added turns (single-shot)
observed: The fallback actually attempts three turns before re-dispatching; it incurs 660 ms of attempted orchestration plus ~200 ms re-dispatch in the unconditional ledger. 'Zero added turns' is only true for the retained-context expectation, not for the fallback's work.
evidence: The same section's ledger gives fallback added orchestration 660 ms + ~200 ms ≈860 ms and 39,395 input tokens.
root_cause: The qualifier 'for retained-context expectation' is dropped in the conditional paragraph.
correction: Say 'incurs zero added retained-context turns for this expectation, though its failed-attempt work is counted in the unconditional ledger.'
acceptance_test: Check that the fallback's 860 ms and 39,395 input are not described as zero work.

quoted_clause: its decision body is kept, not rewritten — the status is updated to superseded, with a link to the successor
observed: The record immediately below has Status: HOLD — screened, not committed. The parenthetical says the status is updated to superseded, which contradicts the displayed HOLD status.
evidence: ADR 0015 Status field: 'HOLD — screened, not committed.' The parenthetical describes a supersession event that has not occurred.
root_cause: The prose describes the future supersession rule as if it were the current state.
correction: Change to 'if and when superseded, the status is updated to superseded with a link to the successor' or remove the clause. Keep the displayed status HOLD.
acceptance_test: The prose and the Status field agree: ADR 0015 is HOLD now; supersession is described conditionally.

quoted_clause: the canonical peak already needs 21 hosts on the KV screen (22 under the case (ii) prefill screen; Ch 16/17/20), so 'adding hosts beyond the 21' misunderstands the scale
observed: The same sentence acknowledges that case (ii) needs 22 hosts. If the governing screen is 22 (or 23 with ρ), then adding a host beyond 21 is exactly what the screen requires; it is not a misunderstanding of scale.
evidence: Ch 20 states 22 raw case-(ii) prefill and 23 with ρ; Ch 25 ADR 0015 R1 also carries 22/34. The alternative rejects 'adding capacity' by treating 21 as the scale, while simultaneously naming 22.
root_cause: The alternative uses the KV-only 21-host screen as if it were the governing screen, then mentions the higher prefill screen without reconciling the argument.
correction: Rewrite the alternative to say: adding hosts beyond the governing screen (21 KV raw, 22 case-(ii) raw, 23 with ρ, 32/34 under full policy) is not the first lever for the KV-capacity problem; FP8 KV relaxes the KV ceiling without commissioning new hardware. Do not dismiss the one host needed to meet case (ii) as a misunderstanding.
acceptance_test: The alternative text uses the governing screen consistently and does not call a required case-(ii) host addition a misunderstanding.

quoted_clause: We measure four things continuously: 1. Gate pass rate ... False-promotion rate ... 2. Canary-to-production time and rollback time ... 3. Model freshness / data staleness ... 4. MTTR for a bad release
observed: The list contains at least six distinct metrics: gate pass rate, false-promotion rate, canary-to-production time, rollback time, model freshness/data staleness, and MTTR. Calling them 'four things' is a counting error.
evidence: The enumerated list itself contains two metrics in item 1 and two in item 2, plus items 3 and 4.
root_cause: Grouped metrics are counted as single 'things' without saying so.
correction: Either say 'we measure four groups of things' and keep the grouping, or say 'we measure six metrics' and enumerate them separately.
acceptance_test: The count word matches the number of enumerated metrics or the text explicitly says it is counting groups.

quoted_clause: Deeper continuous batching on the single host, on top of the baseline sharding, cannot raise throughput here: resident-request capacity is KV-bound at C ≈ 17.5 (Ch 15), so admitting more requests only lengthens the waiting queue and adds prefill interference
observed: The argument treats the KV-resident concurrency ceiling C ≈ 17.5 as if the baseline already operates at that ceiling. A KV ceiling bounds steady-state resident requests; it does not by itself prove that deeper continuous batching cannot raise throughput from a lower baseline batch size up to C.
evidence: Throughput can rise as batch size increases toward the KV-capacity limit even when C is fixed. The claim is only valid once the scheduler is already at C; otherwise deeper batching can improve utilization and throughput before queueing dominates. The text does not state that the baseline is already at C.
root_cause: Capacity ceiling conflated with current operating point.
correction: Qualify the claim: 'once the scheduler is already at the KV-resident ceiling C ≈ 17.5, deeper batching cannot raise steady-state concurrency further; below C it may raise throughput until queueing and prefill interference dominate.' If the capstone assumes the baseline is already at C, state that assumption explicitly.
acceptance_test: The passage distinguishes the KV capacity ceiling from the baseline operating batch/concurrency and states the condition under which deeper batching cannot help.

page_hint: Chapter 26 Table 26-2 cost row and following note
quoted_clause: Cost | $ per query — metered API spend at the canonical 9,200/300 mix, marginal-generation-work share only (DERIVED from FACT inputs, §26.8 — not itself a FACT) | < $0.015 | $0.0076 (API-basis marginal: canonical-mix unit price $0.01164 — a conservative upper bound for this short-prompt leg — × 0.65; self-host all-in is a separate basis, §26.8)
observed: The row mixes two cost bases: 'metered API spend' and 'marginal-generation-work share only.' Multiplying an API unit price by 0.65 produces an API-spend estimate, not a self-hosted marginal-generation-work estimate. The note then calls the modeled cell a marginal-generation-work statement.
evidence: The arithmetic $0.01164 × 0.65 = $0.007566 is an API-basis per-request spend after a 35% cache-hit reduction. It is not the same quantity as self-hosted marginal generation work. The note says the cell is a marginal-generation-work statement, but the cell's inputs are API list prices.
root_cause: Cost-basis labels were carried over from the self-host discussion into an API-priced row.
correction: Either label the row explicitly as 'API-basis marginal spend after cache-hit reduction' and remove 'marginal-generation-work share only,' or compute a separate self-hosted marginal-generation-work figure and keep the API-basis figure in a separate row/column. Do not describe the API-priced cell as a marginal-generation-work estimate.
acceptance_test: The cost row's label, arithmetic, and note all name the same basis; API spend and self-hosted marginal generation work are not conflated.

page_hint: Appendix A post-snapshot notes, multiple paragraphs
observed: Multiple footnote clusters contain stray caret-comma-caret sequences between footnote references, e.g. `[^oct-mt-huginn]^,^[^oct-mt-ouro]`, `[^oct-mt-ouro-code]^,^[^oct-mt-ouro-card]`, and similar patterns in the Intel and video notes.
evidence: The pattern appears repeatedly in the manuscript chunk. It is not standard Markdown footnote syntax and is likely to render as stray superscript punctuation or break footnote parsing.
root_cause: Mechanical insertion or conversion artifact between adjacent footnote references.
correction: Replace each `]^,^[` pattern with a clean separator, e.g. `][^...]` or `]; [^...]`, according to the book's footnote style. Search globally for `^,^`.
acceptance_test: No `^,^` sequences remain; adjacent footnote references render cleanly in the built PDF.

quoted_clause: the Qwen figure is a backbone-only ratio, not a fraction of the deployed parameter inventory; the table is offloadable
observed: The phrase 'the table is offloadable' is ambiguous in context: 'table' refers to Qwen's N-gram embedding table, but the sentence sits near references to the book's tables and the Fig A.1 table.
evidence: The antecedent is separated from the phrase by a long parenthetical and the word 'table' is used elsewhere in the appendix for data tables.
correction: Replace with 'the N-gram embedding table is offloadable' or 'those embedding tables are offloadable.'
acceptance_test: A reader can identify the offloadable object without reconstructing the antecedent from the preceding parenthetical.

issue: The diagram's token labels and central 'append K/V one step later' box can be read as saying that every token's K/V is appended one step after the token is processed, including the token labelled 'end of prefill'. That conflicts with the caption's statement that prompt-token K/V is written during prefill and with the prose on printed p. 15 that a token's K/V enters the cache on the step in which it is the input, not the step in which it is sampled.
evidence: Figure 1.1 labels the first token 'token1 / end of prefill' and routes it through the box 'append K/V / one step later'. The caption says: 'for a generated token, written when that token is next processed as input, one step after it is sampled; prompt-token K/V is written during prefill.' The diagram does not visually separate prompt-token KV writes (during prefill) from generated-token KV writes (one step later). Printed p. 15 states: 'A token's K/V therefore enters the cache on the step in which it is the input, not on the step in which it is sampled.'
acceptance_test: Redraw or relabel Figure 1.1 so that (a) prompt-token K/V is shown as written during prefill, and (b) generated-token K/V is shown as written when that token is next processed as input. The label 'token1 / end of prefill' must be disambiguated as either the last prompt token or the first sampled token, and the 'one step later' annotation must apply only to the generated-token path.

figure: Figure 2.2 — Prefill and decode split by the roofline ridge
issue: The drawn roofline diagonal is not the H100 roofline implied by the figure's own stated inputs. With 989 TFLOPS peak and 3.35 TB/s HBM3, the memory-bound segment should be performance = 3.35e12 × arithmetic intensity, so at 1 FLOP/byte the roof is ~3.35e12 FLOP/s. The chart instead starts the diagonal at ~1e12 FLOP/s at 1 FLOP/byte, making the slope steeper than 1 on the log-log plot and placing the entire memory-bound roof too low.
evidence: Figure 2.2's bottom annotation states: 'H100 SXM, BF16 dense: 989 TFLOPS peak, 3.35 TB/s HBM3 → ridge at 295 FLOP/byte'. The roofline equation is attainable performance = min(peak, bandwidth × arithmetic intensity). At arithmetic intensity = 1 FLOP/byte, bandwidth × intensity = 3.35e12 FLOP/s. The drawn diagonal visibly starts at the 1e12 gridline at x = 1, not at ~3.35e12. The ridge point is drawn at ~295 FLOP/byte and 989 TFLOPS, so the line from (1, 1e12) to (295, 989e12) has log-log slope ≈ 1.21, not the required slope of 1 for a bandwidth-limited roofline segment.
acceptance_test: Replot the memory-bound roofline segment through (1, 3.35e12) and (295, 989e12) on the same log-log axes, or explicitly state that the drawn diagonal is a schematic not to scale. If the diagonal is retained as a schematic, remove the quantitative '3.35 TB/s HBM3 → ridge at 295 FLOP/byte' claim from the same visual or label the diagonal as 'schematic, not to scale'.

figure: Figure 2.2 — Prefill and decode split by the roofline ridge
issue: The blue 'prefill' marker is not plotted at the canonical prefill arithmetic intensity stated in the caption (~9.2K FLOP/byte). On the log x-axis it sits visibly closer to the middle of the 10^3–10^4 decade, roughly a few thousand FLOP/byte, rather than near the 10^4 edge where ~9.2K would fall.
evidence: The caption states: 'arithmetic intensity places the canonical prefill point ~9.2K FLOP/byte, well to the right of the ~295 ridge'. The x-axis is logarithmic with ticks at 1, 10, 100, 1000, 10000. The blue triangle labelled 'prefill' is drawn well to the left of the 10000 tick, at approximately the middle of the 1000–10000 decade. A value of 9.2K would be at ~0.96 of that decade, very close to the 10000 tick.
acceptance_test: Move the prefill marker to x ≈ 9.2×10^3 FLOP/byte on the log axis, or change the caption to state the value actually plotted. If the marker is intentionally schematic, label it 'schematic position' and remove the precise '~9.2K' claim from the same figure.

issue: Panel B draws a solid bracket under the partially accepted canvas (A ? C ?), visually marking it as finalized prefix state, while the caption says prompt-state reuse is not assumed and accepted IDs alone do not establish reusable K/V.
evidence: Caption: 'Here, accepted IDs stay fixed; prompt-state reuse is not assumed.' and 'Solid brackets identify finalized prefix state; accepted token IDs alone do not establish reusable K/V.' Panel B shows a solid bracket beneath the A ? C ? canvas.
acceptance_test: Remove the solid bracket in panel B or replace it with a dashed/annotated marker that explicitly says 'no reusable K/V'; verify no solid bracket appears where prompt-state reuse is not assumed.

issue: The 'Five selection surfaces' box includes 'retrieve-vs-generate', but the caption calls these 'model-selection dimensions'; retrieve-vs-generate is a system/architecture split, not a model-selection surface.
evidence: Figure box: 'quality · latency · KV cache · $/tok · retrieve-vs-generate'; caption: 'The five surfaces are the model-selection dimensions'; the diagram itself splits into retrieval and generation legs.
acceptance_test: Either rename the box/caption to 'system-selection surfaces' or replace 'retrieve-vs-generate' with a genuine model-selection dimension and move the retrieve-vs-generate decision to the split arrows.

issue: The Serving metrics box includes 'queue depth (scheduler)', but the prose on the facing page explicitly says queue depth is not a serving metric; the box also omits ITL, which the prose lists.
evidence: Page 96: 'Queue depth is not one of them: it is a scheduler state, a leading indicator that helps explain these serving metrics.' Figure 6.1 Serving metrics: 'TTFT · TPOT · goodput · queue depth (scheduler)'.
acceptance_test: Move queue depth outside the Serving metrics box (e.g., a separate scheduler-state annotation) and add ITL to the Serving metrics list; ensure caption and prose agree.

issue: Caption calls the second dimension 'Traffic / concurrency' while the figure labels it 'Request rate & arrival pattern'; the two are related but not identical, creating terminology drift.
evidence: Figure left box: 'Request rate & arrival pattern'; caption: 'Traffic / concurrency → concurrency & batching'.
acceptance_test: Use one label consistently in figure and caption, e.g., 'Request rate & arrival pattern (traffic/concurrency)'.

issue: The green forward arrow from DERIVED to PATTERN is labeled 'validate', but validation is a measurement/feedback action, not a forward selection step. The red feedback arrow from PATTERN back to ASSUMPTION is the actual measurement loop. The caption says 'The loop closes by measurement — an assumption that fails validation returns to box 1 for adjustment', which places validation on the feedback path, not on the DERIVED→PATTERN arrow.
evidence: Green arrow label: 'validate p99 < 300 ms (target ≤ 800 ms)'. Red arrow labels: 'feedback' and 'adjust + pick pattern'. Caption: 'The loop closes by measurement — an assumption that fails validation returns to box 1 for adjustment, and only measured FACTs enter the decision.'
acceptance_test: Move the 'validate' label to the feedback arrow or add an explicit measurement/validation box on the return path. The forward arrow should be labeled as a target/selection criterion (e.g., 'select pattern to meet criterion'), not as validation.

figure: Figure 26.1 — Workload fingerprints on the six axes
issue: The critical caveat 'per-axis 0-1 scale; compare within an axis, not across axes' is set in small, light gray type below the legend. At print size it is easy to miss, yet it is the only in-figure warning that prevents a reader from comparing bars across different axes as if they were a single measured scale. The y-axis label 'Authored intensity (0-1)' further invites cross-axis comparison.
evidence: The note appears below the legend in small gray text: 'per-axis 0-1 scale; compare within an axis, not across axes.' The y-axis is labeled 'Authored intensity (0-1)'. The prose on the next page clarifies that the scores are subjective authored values, but the figure itself must carry that warning legibly.
acceptance_test: Increase the caveat to at least the 8 pt figure-annotation floor and darken it, or move it into the caption. A reader viewing only the figure should immediately understand that the six axes are separate 0–1 scales and that bar heights are not comparable across axes.

figure: Figure 25.1 — The Anatomy of an Architecture Decision Record
issue: The top ADR is labeled 'kept, not edited', while the caption says 'only the Status line is updated when a successor supersedes it.' A careful reader can read 'not edited' as contradicting the status update. The intended meaning is that the body is kept unchanged while the status is updated.
evidence: Top box: 'ADR-001 (superseded)' with gray italic label 'kept, not edited'. Caption: 'the body is never rewritten, and only the Status line is updated when a successor supersedes it.'
acceptance_test: Change the label to something unambiguous such as 'body kept; status updated' or 'kept on file (body unchanged)'. The figure and caption should agree without requiring the caption to rescue the label.
